title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: PLAC not Scripture's usual reference; only reconcilable sense
pass_a_gloss: Placeus answers that the question here is not what Scripture is accustomed to refer to God's judgment; as he already observed, it never in any place refers the propagation of original sin to God's judgment. Ask only in what sense—Scripture not resisting and reason allowing—it can be referred. He sees no other sense reconcilable with Scripture and right reason besides the one he set out in this place and in this same Manuscript at the end of cap. 12 and a little before the middle of cap. 13.
pass_b_english: PLAC. First, it is not asked in this place what Scripture is accustomed to refer to God's judgment. For, as I have already observed, it has in no place referred the propagation of original sin to God's judgment. It is asked only in what sense, Scripture not resisting, and reason allowing, it can be referred. Certainly I see no other sense that can be reconciled with Scripture and right reason besides that which I have set out in this place and at the end of cap. 12 and a little before the middle of cap. 13 of this same Manuscript.
source_text: PLAC. Primum non quaeritur hoc loco quid soleat Scriptura ad Dei judicium referre. Non enim, ut iam observavi, ullo loco propagationem originalis peccati ad Dei judicium retulit. Quaeritur tantum quo sensu non repugnante Scriptura, & rationi possit referri. Alium certe sensum, qui cum Scriptura & recta ratione conciliari possit, non video, praeter eum, quem hoc loco & in fine cap. 12. & paulo ante medium cap. 13. huius ipsius Manuscripti exposui.
